title: To amend title 36, United States Code, to make certain improvements in the congressional charter of the Disabled American Veterans.
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the House on November 30, 2015. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

(Sec. 1) This bill states that Disabled American Veterans (the corporation) is organized exclusively for charitable and educational purposes, and includes among its purposes: (1) education of the public about the sacrifices and needs of disabled veterans, and (2) education of disabled veterans about the benefits and resources available to them.

On dissolution or final liquidation of the corporation, any assets remaining after the discharge or satisfactory provision for the discharge of all liabilities shall be transferred to the Department of Veterans Affairs for the care of disabled veterans.

summary.headline: This law updates the federal charter of the Disabled American Veterans group, clarifying its charitable purposes and where its leftover assets go if it dissolves.
summary.what_it_does: The law amends the federal charter for Disabled American Veterans, a nonprofit corporation. It says the group exists for charitable and educational purposes, including teaching the public about the sacrifices and needs of disabled veterans and teaching disabled veterans about benefits and resources available to them. It also says that if the group dissolves, any leftover assets after paying all debts go to the Department of Veterans Affairs to care for disabled veterans.

who_it_affects.how: The charter now spells out the group's educational and charitable purposes, including informing disabled veterans about available benefits and resources.
If the organization dissolves, its remaining assets must go to the Department of Veterans Affairs for veterans' care.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on March 18, 2016, and the summary does not give a separate effective date.
